questions.question: A ball is released from rest at the top of an inclined smooth plane of length 5 cm. After reaching the bottom it travels horizontally on a smooth surface. How much distance will it travel horizontally? (Neglect the frictional forces as both the plane and surface are smooth)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Infinite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The motion of the ball is governed by **Newton’s First Law of Motion**, also known as the **Law of Inertia**. This law states that an object will remain in its state of rest or **uniform motion** in a straight line unless acted upon by an **external unbalanced force**.
 
• In the given scenario, the ball starts from rest at the top of a **5 cm** long **smooth inclined plane**. As it moves down, **potential energy** is converted into **kinetic energy**, and the ball reaches the bottom with a specific **velocity**.
 
• Once the ball reaches the **horizontal smooth surface**, there is no **frictional force** or air resistance (as the problem states to neglect them). Because the surface is **smooth**, the **coefficient of friction** is **zero**.
 
• On a horizontal plane, the **force of gravity** acts vertically downwards and is balanced by the **normal reaction force** acting upwards. Therefore, there is no **net force** acting on the ball in the horizontal direction of motion.
 
• According to the equation of motion, if the **net force** is **zero**, the **acceleration** is also **zero** (based on **Newton's Second Law**, F = ma). This means the ball will maintain a **constant velocity** indefinitely. Since it never stops, the **distance** it travels horizontally is **Infinite**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Galileo’s Experiment on Inertia:**
 
 
• The concept of **Inertia** was first extensively studied by **Galileo Galilei**. He conducted experiments with double inclined planes.
 
• He observed that if a ball is released from one side, it climbs to the **same height** on the other side. If the angle of the second slope is reduced, the ball travels a **longer distance** to reach that same height.
 
• Galileo concluded that if the second plane were made **horizontal** (angle of **0 degrees**), the ball would continue to move **forever** in an attempt to reach its original height, provided there is no **friction**.
 
 
 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion:**
 
 
• It defines **Inertia**, which is the inherent property of a body to resist changes in its state of motion.
 
• There are three types of inertia: **Inertia of rest**, **Inertia of motion**, and **Inertia of direction**.
 
• In this problem, the ball exhibits **inertia of motion** once it leaves the incline and enters the horizontal path.
 
 
 
• **Role of Friction:**
 
 
• In **real-world conditions**, surfaces are never perfectly **smooth**. **Frictional forces** and **air resistance** act as external unbalanced forces that eventually bring the ball to rest.
 
• However, in **ideal physics problems** where surfaces are described as **smooth**, we assume the **frictional force** is **0 Newtons**, leading to **theoretical infinite motion**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **length of the incline (5 cm)** determines the **final velocity** at the bottom but does not affect the **total distance** traveled on an infinite smooth horizontal plane.
 
• The **velocity (v)** at the bottom of the incline can be calculated using **v² = u² + 2as** or **conservation of energy** (mgh = 1/2 mv²), but since there is no deceleration on the horizontal part, this velocity remains **constant**.
 
• The horizontal distance **(d)** is calculated by **d = velocity × time**. As time **(t)** tends toward **infinity** in the absence of a stopping force, the distance also becomes **Infinite**.

questions.question: In humans, which parent determines the sex of the child?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Father**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• In humans, the determination of the sex of a child is a **genetic process** governed by the **23rd pair** of chromosomes, known as the **sex chromosomes**.

• Human beings have a total of **46 chromosomes** or **23 pairs**. Out of these, **22 pairs** are **autosomes** (identical in both males and females), and the **last pair** defines the biological sex.

• The female genetic makeup consists of two **X chromosomes** (**XX**). Consequently, all **gametes** (eggs) produced by a mother contain only an **X chromosome**.

• The male genetic makeup consists of one **X chromosome** and one **Y chromosome** (**XY**). This means the **father** is **heterogametic**, producing two types of **sperm**: one carrying the **X chromosome** and the other carrying the **Y chromosome**.

• The sex of the child depends entirely on which type of sperm fertilizes the egg. If a sperm with an **X chromosome** fuses with the egg, the resulting child will be **XX (female)**. If a sperm with a **Y chromosome** fuses with the egg, the child will be **XY (male)**. ***Hence, the father is the parent who determines the sex of the child.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Chromosomal Basis of Sex**:

• The mechanism where specific chromosomes determine the sex of an individual is called **sex determination**. In humans, this is the **XY system**.

• During **meiosis**, the chromosome pairs separate so that each **gamete** receives only one chromosome from each pair.

• Since the **ovum** (egg) always contributes an **X**, the **zygote's** sex is determined at the moment of **fertilization** by the **male gamete**.

• **Probability of Sex**:

• Statistically, there is a **50% chance** of having a boy and a **50% chance** of having a girl in every pregnancy, as the ratio of **X-carrying sperm** to **Y-carrying sperm** is **1:1**.

• **Other Systems in Nature**:

• Not all organisms follow the **XY system**. For instance, in **birds**, the system is **ZW**, where the **female** (ZW) is the **heterogametic** sex and determines the sex of the offspring, while the **male** is **ZZ**.

• In some **reptiles**, sex is determined by **environmental factors** like the **incubation temperature** of the eggs rather than genetics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **The SRY Gene**:

• The **Y chromosome** contains a specific gene called the **SRY gene** (**Sex-determining Region Y**).

• This gene is responsible for the initiation of **male sex determination** by triggering the development of undifferentiated gonads into **testes**.

• In the absence of a **Y chromosome** (and thus the **SRY gene**), the biological default pathway leads to the development of **ovaries** and a female phenotype.

• **Historical Context**:

• The chromosomal theory of sex determination was discovered in the early **20th century** (around **1905**) by American geneticists **Nettie Stevens** and **Edmund Beecher Wilson**.

• Their work shifted the understanding of heredity from vague external factors to specific **microscopic structures** within the **cell nucleus**.

• **Misconceptions**:

• In many cultures historically, mothers were wrongly blamed for not bearing a male child. Scientific evidence clearly shows that the **mother's genetic contribution** to sex is **constant (X)**, and the **father's contribution** is the **variable factor**.

</ul

questions.question: What happens to the gravitational force between two objects, if the distance between them is doubled and everything else remains the same?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The force becomes one-fourth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The gravitational force between two bodies is determined by **Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation**, which states that the force is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the **square of the distance** between them.
 
• Mathematically, the formula is expressed as **F = G (m1m2 / r²)**, where **F** is the gravitational force, **G** is the universal gravitational constant, **m1** and **m2** are the masses of the two objects, and **r** is the distance between their centers.
 
• According to the **Inverse Square Law** relationship, if the distance **r** is **doubled** (becomes **2r**), the new force **F'** becomes proportional to **1 / (2r)²**, which simplifies to **1 / 4r²**.
 
• This calculation shows that the new force is exactly **one-fourth (1/4)** of the original force. *Hence, the statement that the force becomes one-fourth is correct.*
 
• Conversely, if the distance were halved, the force would increase by **four times**, illustrating the significant impact of distance on gravitational attraction compared to mass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation:** Formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** and published in **1687** in his work **"Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica"**. It provides a mathematical description of the gravitational pull that every object in the universe exerts on every other object.
 
• **The Gravitational Constant (G):** This is a fundamental physical constant. Its value was first accurately measured by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798**. The modern accepted value is approximately **6.674 x 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²**.
 
• **Mass and Force Relationship:** While distance has an inverse square relationship, the force is **directly proportional** to the masses. If the mass of one object is **doubled**, the gravitational force also **doubles**, provided the distance remains constant.
 
• **Range of Gravity:** Gravity is a **long-range force** that exists between all objects with mass, regardless of how far apart they are, though it becomes negligibly small at extreme astronomical distances.
 
• **Significance in the Solar System:** This law explains why **planets orbit the Sun** and why the **Moon orbits the Earth**. It also accounts for the phenomenon of **tides**, which are caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun on Earth's oceans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Weight vs. Gravitational Force:** The **weight** of an object on Earth is actually the gravitational force exerted by the Earth on that object. It is calculated using **W = mg**, where **g** is the acceleration due to gravity (approximately **9.8 m/s²**).
 
• **Vector Nature:** Gravitational force is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**. The direction of the force is always along the line joining the centers of the two masses and is always **attractive**.
 
• **Universal Applicability:** It is called a "Universal" law because it applies to everything from small **terrestrial objects** to massive **celestial bodies** like stars and galaxies.
 
• **Center of Mass:** For spherical objects with uniform density, the distance **r** is measured specifically from the **center of mass** of one object to the center of mass of the other.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the phrase “the DNA copies generated will be similar, but may not be identical”?

options.text: Each DNA copy is totally unrelated.
The original DNA is destroyed after copying.
DNA copies may have slight differences.
All DNA copies are identical clones.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DNA copies may have slight differences**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of **DNA replication** is a **biochemical reaction**. In biology, no chemical reaction is **100%** absolutely reliable or accurate every single time.
 
• When a cell reproduces, it creates a copy of its **DNA** through these chemical processes. Because of the inherent nature of these reactions, the resulting DNA strands are very **similar** to the original but may contain minor **alterations**. ***Hence, the statement that DNA copies may have slight differences is correct.***
 
• If each DNA copy were **totally unrelated**, the offspring would not belong to the same **species** as the parent, which contradicts the fundamental principles of **heredity**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• During replication, the original DNA acts as a **template**. It is not **destroyed**; rather, it provides the structural information for the synthesis of the new strand. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The idea that all DNA copies are **identical clones** is biologically improbable due to the occurrence of **mutations** and copying errors. These "errors" are actually the basis for **diversity** in a population. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The phrase “similar, but may not be identical” acknowledges the existence of **biological variations** that occur during the transfer of **genetic information** from one generation to the next.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid):** It is the **genetic material** found in the **nucleus** of almost all living organisms. It carries the **blueprints** for the **body design** and functioning of the cell.
 
• **DNA Replication:** This is the process by which a **double-stranded** DNA molecule is copied to produce two identical DNA molecules. It is a critical part of **cell division** (mitosis and meiosis).
 
• **The Role of Variations:** Variations are the differences that exist between individuals of the same species. These variations are necessary for **evolution**. If an environment changes drastically (e.g., **global warming**), these slight differences might allow some individuals to **survive** while others perish.
 
• **Historical Context:** The **double helix** structure of DNA was famously proposed by **James Watson** and **Francis Crick** in **1953**, which helped scientists understand how DNA could "unzip" and **replicate** itself.
 
• **Genetic Stability:** While variation is important, **stability** is also required. If the DNA copying process had too many errors, the resulting **cellular apparatus** would fail to function, leading to the **death** of the new cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mutation:** A **mutation** is a permanent change in the **nucleotide sequence** of DNA. These can be caused by **copying errors**, **UV radiation**, or chemicals.
 
• **Niche and Adaptation:** DNA copying consistency allows organisms to occupy a specific **ecological niche**. Variations allow them to **adapt** when that niche undergoes **environmental shifts**.
 
• **Asexual vs Sexual Reproduction:** In **asexual reproduction**, the variation is minimal because there is only one parent, whereas in **sexual reproduction**, variations are increased because genetic material from **two different individuals** is combined.
 
• **Enzymatic Control:** The replication process is managed by enzymes like **DNA polymerase**, which has a **proofreading** function to minimize errors, though it is not perfect.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares vacuoles in plant and animal cells?

options.text: Both plant and animal cells have equal-sized vacuoles
Animal cells have larger vacuoles than plant cells
Plant cells have large vacuoles, animal cells have small ones
Vacuoles are absent in both plant and animal cells

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plant cells have large vacuoles, animal cells have small ones**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vacuoles** are membrane-bound organelles found in the cells of plants, animals, fungi, and some protists, acting primarily as storage bubbles.
 
• In **plant cells**, there is typically one very large **central vacuole** that can occupy up to **90%** of the cell's total volume. This large size is a defining characteristic of mature plant cells.
 
• In **animal cells**, vacuoles are much **smaller** in size and often **temporary**. They are distributed throughout the cytoplasm and are frequently involved in transport or short-term storage.
 
• The large central vacuole in plants is essential for maintaining **turgor pressure**, which provides structural support and keeps the plant upright by pushing the **cytoplasm** against the **cell wall**.
 
• The statement that plant cells have large vacuoles and animal cells have small ones accurately describes the morphological difference between the two. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tonoplast:** The specialized membrane that surrounds the central vacuole in **plant cells** is known as the **tonoplast**. It facilitates the active transport of ions and other materials into the vacuole, maintaining a concentration gradient.
 
• **Cell Sap:** The fluid contained within the plant vacuole is called **cell sap**. It is a mixture of **water**, **amino acids**, **sugars**, **waste products**, and vital mineral salts.
 
• **Anthocyanins:** Some plant vacuoles contain pigments like **anthocyanins**, which are responsible for the **red**, **purple**, and **blue** colors seen in many flowers and fruits, aiding in pollination and seed dispersal.
 
• **Functions in Animals:** In animal cells, vacuoles (often called **vesicles**) are involved in **exocytosis** (expelling waste) and **endocytosis** (bringing materials into the cell). They play a key role in the **digestive processes** of simple organisms.
 
• **Contractile Vacuoles:** Some freshwater protists like **Amoeba** possess **contractile vacuoles**, which collect and pump out excess water to prevent the cell from bursting, a vital process for **osmoregulation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Structural Difference:** Unlike plant cells which have a **permanent** large central vacuole, the vacuoles in animal cells are often **transient** and can form or disappear based on the cell's metabolic needs.
 
• **Discovery:** Vacuoles were first observed by **Antonie van Leeuwenhoek** in **1676**, though their specific functions in plant turgidity were understood much later.
 
• **Waste Management:** In plants, the vacuole acts as a **waste disposal** site, isolating materials that might be harmful or toxic to the rest of the cell's **organelles**.
 
• **Growth Mechanism:** Plants grow by absorbing water into the central vacuole, which expands the cell with minimal investment in new **cytoplasm**, allowing for rapid **cell elongation**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following types of reproduction ensures that offspring inherit features from both parents in animals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sexual reproduction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: In a substitution reaction involving an alkane, what happens to the hydrogen atoms of the alkane molecule?

options.text: They are replaced by other atoms or groups of atoms.
They are added to the molecule to form a larger chain.
They are completely removed to form double bonds.
They react with oxygen to form water.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are replaced by other atoms or groups of atoms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **substitution reaction** is a fundamental type of chemical reaction where one functional group or atom in a chemical compound is replaced by another atom or group of atoms.
 
• In the case of **alkanes**, which are **saturated hydrocarbons**, the carbon atoms are already bonded to the maximum number of hydrogen atoms through **single covalent bonds**.
 
• During a substitution reaction involving an alkane, one or more **hydrogen atoms** are removed and **replaced** by atoms of another element, most commonly **halogens** (Chlorine, Bromine, etc.). *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• These reactions do not result in the growth of the carbon chain length through simple addition, which is a characteristic of **addition reactions** found in **unsaturated hydrocarbons** like alkenes. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• The hydrogen atoms are not simply removed to form double bonds; the formation of double bonds from alkanes is typically classified as a **dehydrogenation** or **elimination reaction**, which usually requires high temperatures or specific catalysts. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• While alkanes do react with oxygen to form water and carbon dioxide, this process is known as **combustion** (an oxidation reaction), not a substitution reaction. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Alkanes:** Alkanes are often called **paraffins** (Latin: parum affinis = little affinity) because they are relatively unreactive under normal conditions due to the stability of **C-C** and **C-H** sigma bonds.
 
• **Halogenation of Alkanes:** This is the most common substitution reaction for alkanes. It typically occurs in the presence of **ultraviolet (UV) light** or **diffused sunlight**, which provides the energy needed to break the bonds of the halogen molecules.
 
• **Reaction Mechanism:** The substitution reaction in alkanes follows a **free-radical mechanism**. This process involves three distinct steps: **initiation** (creation of radicals), **propagation** (reaction of radicals with alkanes), and **termination** (radicals combining to form stable molecules).
 
• **Example:** When **Methane (CH₄)** reacts with **Chlorine (Cl₂)** in sunlight, a hydrogen atom is replaced by a chlorine atom to form **Chloromethane (CH₃Cl)** and **Hydrogen Chloride (HCl)**. If chlorine is in excess, the reaction can continue until all four hydrogen atoms are replaced, resulting in **Carbon Tetrachloride (CCl₄)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reactivity Order:** The reactivity of halogens toward alkanes in substitution reactions follows the order: **Fluorine > Chlorine > Bromine > Iodine**. Fluorination is often too explosive to control, while iodination is very slow and reversible.
 
• **Homologous Series:** Alkanes form a **homologous series** with the general formula **CnH₂n+₂**. As the molecular mass increases in the series, the **boiling point** and **melting point** also increase due to stronger Van der Waals forces.
 
• **Industrial Use:** Substitution reactions are vital in the chemical industry for producing **alkyl halides**, which serve as precursors for manufacturing polymers, refrigerants, and pharmaceuticals.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains why dry HCl gas does NOT change the colour of dry litmus paper, but aqueous HCl does?

options.text: Water reacts with litmus, not HCl.
Litmus paper only works in the presence of light.
HCl only releases H⁺ ions when dissolved in water.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**HCl only releases H+ ions when dissolved in water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acids** are defined by their ability to produce **Hydrogen ions (H+)** when dissolved in a solvent like **water**. In the case of **Hydrogen Chloride (HCl)**, the dry gas consists of covalent molecules that do not contain free ions.
 
• When **dry HCl gas** is passed over **dry litmus paper**, there is no **water** present to facilitate the **ionization** process. Consequently, no **H+ ions** are released, and the litmus paper does not change its **color**.
 
• In an **aqueous solution**, **HCl** molecules react with **water (H2O)** to form **Hydronium ions (H3O+)** and **Chloride ions (Cl-)**. This process is known as **dissociation**. ***Hence, statement 3 is the correct explanation.***
 
• The **acidic properties** of a substance are solely manifested through these **H+ ions**. **Litmus paper**, which is a plant-based indicator, requires the presence of these ions to undergo a chemical change from **blue to red**.
 
• **Water reacts with litmus, not HCl**: This is incorrect because water alone is **neutral** (pH 7) and does not change the color of litmus paper; it is the **HCl** that provides the acidic nature once dissolved. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Litmus paper only works in the presence of light**: The reaction of litmus is a **chemical acid-base reaction**, not a photochemical one, meaning it does not depend on **light**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Dry HCl gas is non-acidic**: While **dry HCl** does not show acidic behavior, it is technically still an **acidic gas** by chemical nature (it is a proton donor). The lack of **moisture** simply prevents the manifestation of its acidity. ***Hence, statement 4 is partially misleading and not the best scientific explanation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Arrhenius Theory**: This **scientific theory** proposed by **Svante Arrhenius** in **1884** states that **acids** are substances that dissociate in **aqueous solutions** to yield **hydrogen ions**.
 
• **Litmus**: It is a **natural indicator** extracted from **Lichens** (specifically species like **Roccella tinctoria**). It turns **red** in **acidic conditions** (pH below 4.5) and **blue** in **alkaline conditions** (pH above 8.3).
 
• **Hydrogen Chloride (HCl)**: It is a **colorless gas** at **room temperature**. When dissolved in water, it forms **Hydrochloric Acid**, which is a **strong mineral acid** widely used in **industries** for **pickling steel** and **regulating pH**.
 
• **Polarity of Water**: **Water** is a **polar solvent**. The **electrostatic attraction** between the partial charges of **water molecules** and the **HCl** molecules is what pulls the **H** and **Cl** apart, allowing **ionization** to occur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hydronium Ion**: It is important to note that **H+ ions** do not exist alone in **water**. They quickly combine with **water molecules** to form **Hydronium ions (H3O+)**. The equation is represented as: **HCl + H2O → H3O+ + Cl-**.
 
• **Moisture Requirement**: If you use **moist litmus paper** with **dry HCl gas**, the gas will dissolve in the **water** present on the paper, forming **ions** and causing the **color** to change to **red** immediately.
 
• **Safety**: **HCl gas** is highly **corrosive** and **toxic**. It can react with the **moisture** in the **human respiratory system** to form **acid**, which can cause severe **irritation** or **burns**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the main function of epithelial tissue in animals?

options.text: It covers and protects organs and cavities of the body.
It provides mechanical support and shape to organs.
It connects muscles and bones for body movement.
It transports gases and hormones throughout the body.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It covers and protects organs and cavities of the body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Epithelial tissue** is the simplest tissue in the **animal body** and serves as a primary protective layer.
 
• Its main function is to **cover the external surface** of the body and line the **internal organs** and **body cavities**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• It acts as a **barrier** to keep different body systems separate, ensuring that the internal environment of various organs remains distinct.
 
• The cells of epithelial tissue are **tightly packed** and form a **continuous sheet**. They have almost no **intercellular spaces** between them, which enhances their protective capability.
 
• Anything entering or leaving the body must cross at least one layer of the **epithelium**. Because of this, the **permeability** of the cells of various epithelia plays a critical role in regulating the exchange of materials between the body and the external environment.
 
• Common examples of locations where epithelial tissue is found include the **skin**, the **lining of the mouth**, the **lining of blood vessels**, **lung alveoli**, and **kidney tubules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Epithelial Tissue:**
 
 
• **Simple Squamous Epithelium:** These cells are extremely **thin and flat**, forming a delicate lining. They are found in sites where **transport of substances** occurs through a selectively permeable surface, such as the **oesophagus** and the **lining of the mouth**.
 
• **Stratified Squamous Epithelium:** Found in the **skin**, these cells are arranged in **many layers** to prevent **wear and tear**.
 
• **Ciliated Columnar Epithelium:** Found in the **respiratory tract**, these cells have hair-like projections called **cilia** that move to clear **mucus** forward.
 
• **Cuboidal Epithelium:** These cube-shaped cells provide **mechanical support** and are found in **kidney tubules** and the ducts of **salivary glands**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect*** as mechanical support is a secondary function specific to cuboidal types, not the primary general function of all epithelial tissues.
 
• **Glandular Epithelium:** Sometimes a portion of epithelial tissue folds inward to form a **multicellular gland** for **secretion**.
 
 
 
• **Other Animal Tissues:**
 
 
• **Connective Tissue:** This tissue connects different organs and provides structural support. For example, **tendons** connect muscles to bones, and **ligaments** connect bones to bones. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Fluid Connective Tissue:** **Blood** is a type of connective tissue that has a fluid matrix called **plasma**. It is responsible for **transporting gases, digested food, hormones, and waste materials** to different parts of the body. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Muscular Tissue:** Responsible for **movement** in our body, consisting of elongated cells called **muscle fibres**.
 
• **Nervous Tissue:** Specialized for being stimulated and then **transmitting the stimulus** very rapidly from one place to another within the body.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• All epithelium is usually separated from the underlying tissue by an **extracellular fibrous basement membrane**.
 
• The **skin**, which protects the body, is also made of **squamous epithelium** arranged in patterns of layers.
 
• In the **intestine**, where **absorption** and **secretion** occur, tall epithelial cells called **columnar epithelium** are present to facilitate movement across the epithelial barrier.
 
• The study of tissues is known as **Histology**.
</ul

questions.question: If an electric heater consumes 1000 W of power, how much electrical energy does it use in 1 hour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 kWh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **electrical energy** consumed by an appliance can be calculated using the formula: **Energy = Power x Time**.
 
• In this problem, the **power (P)** of the electric heater is given as **1000 W** and the **time (t)** is given as **1 hour**.
 
• Multiplying these values, we get: **1000 Watts x 1 hour = 1000 Watt-hours (Wh)**.
 
• By definition, **1000 Watt-hours** is equal to **1 kilowatt-hour (1 kWh)**, which is the standard unit for measuring energy consumption. ***Hence, the correct answer is 1 kWh.***
 
• If we were to convert this into the **SI unit of energy (Joules)**, **1 kWh** would be equal to **1000 Watts x 3600 seconds**, which results in **3,600,000 Joules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kilowatt-hour (kWh)**:
 
 
• The **kilowatt-hour** is the **commercial unit** of electrical energy used by electricity boards to calculate bills.
 
• One unit of electricity consumed in a household refers to **1 kWh** of energy used.
 
• It represents the amount of energy dissipated by a **1000-watt** appliance working continuously for **one hour**.
 
 
 
• **Power and its Units**:
 
 
• **Power** is defined as the rate at which **work is done** or **energy is consumed**.
 
• The **SI unit** of power is the **Watt (W)**, named after **James Watt**. **1 Watt** is equivalent to **1 Joule per second (1 J/s)**.
 
• For high-power devices like **heaters**, **motors**, and **engines**, power is often measured in **kilowatts (kW)** or **Horsepower (hp)**, where **1 hp** is approximately **746 Watts**.
 
 
 
• **Joule (J)**:
 
 
• The **Joule** is the **SI unit of energy**. It is a very small unit compared to the **kilowatt-hour**.
 
• To convert **kWh** to **Joules**, you multiply by **3.6 million (3,600,000)** because there are **3600 seconds** in an hour and **1000 Watts** in a kilowatt.
 
 
 
• **Practical Examples**:
 
 
• An **LED bulb** rated at **10 W** would take **100 hours** to consume **1 kWh** of energy.
 
• In contrast, a heavy-duty **air conditioner** rated at **2000 W (2 kW)** would consume **1 kWh** in just **30 minutes**.
 
• Understanding these ratings helps in managing **household energy efficiency** and reducing **electricity costs**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following symbols represents a rheostat?

options.text: A circle with a 'V' inside it.
A zigzag line with an arrow which is drawn across it.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A zigzag line with an arrow which is drawn across it**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **rheostat** is an electrical instrument used to control **current** by varying the **resistance** in a circuit without changing the voltage source.
 
• The standard circuit symbol for a **rheostat** is a **zigzag line** (which represents resistance) with a **diagonal arrow** drawn across it or an arrow pointing down onto the zigzag. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• It functions as a **variable resistor** and is typically constructed using a resistive wire (like **manganin** or **constantan**) wrapped around an insulating ceramic core, with a sliding contact.
 
• By moving the **slider** (the arrow in the symbol), the effective length of the wire through which the current passes changes, thereby altering the total **resistance** of the circuit according to the formula **R = ρ(L/A)**.
 
• In **Ohm's Law** experiments, a **rheostat** is frequently used to adjust the current flowing through a conductor to observe the corresponding change in **potential difference**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ammeter:**
 
 
• Represented by an **'A' inside a circle**.
 
• It is a device used to measure the **electric current** in a circuit in **Amperes**.
 
• It has **low resistance** and is always connected in **series** with the circuit component. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Voltmeter:**
 
 
• Represented by a **circle with a 'V' inside it**.
 
• It is used to measure the **potential difference** (voltage) between two points in an electrical circuit.
 
• It has **high resistance** and is always connected in **parallel** across the points where the voltage is to be measured. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Fixed Resistor:**
 
 
• Represented by a simple **zigzag line**.
 
• It provides a specific, unchanging amount of **electrical resistance** to the flow of current.
 
• The unit of measurement for resistance is the **Ohm (Ω)**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Galvanometer:**
 
 
• Represented by a **'G' inside a circle**.
 
• It is an electromechanical instrument used for **detecting** and indicating the **presence and direction** of small electric currents.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Potentiometer vs. Rheostat:** While both are variable resistors, a **potentiometer** is typically used as a **voltage divider** using three terminals, whereas a **rheostat** is used to control **current** using only two terminals.
 
• **Applications:** Rheostats are used in **motor speed control**, **light dimmers**, and older **volume control** knobs in radio sets.
 
• **Ohm’s Law:** The relationship **V = IR** dictates that if **voltage (V)** is constant, increasing the **resistance (R)** using a rheostat will decrease the **current (I)**.
 
• **Safety:** When using a **rheostat** in laboratory experiments, it is vital to ensure it can handle the **wattage** or heat generated by the current to prevent damage to the component.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is /are true regarding the work done by a constant force acting on a body?

(i) The work done by the force can never be zero.
(ii) If the direction of the force and displacement of the body is same, the work done will be positive.
(iii) The S.I. unit of work done is joule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (ii) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work Done Definition**: In physics, work is said to be done when a **force** acts upon an object to cause a **displacement**. It is mathematically expressed as **W = Fs cosθ**, where **F** is the force, **s** is the displacement, and **θ** is the angle between the force and displacement vectors.
 
• **Analysis of Statement (i)**: The work done by a force can be **zero** under three conditions: if the **force** applied is zero, if the **displacement** is zero, or if the force acts **perpendicularly** (at an angle of **90 degrees**) to the direction of motion (since **cos 90 = 0**). Examples include a person standing still with a heavy load or a satellite moving in a circular orbit where the gravitational force is perpendicular to the velocity. ***Hence, statement (i) is incorrect.***
 
• **Analysis of Statement (ii)**: If the **force** and the **displacement** are in the **same direction**, the angle **θ** is **0 degrees**. Because the value of **cos 0** is **1**, the work done is **positive**. This is common when pushing an object across a floor in the direction of the push. ***Hence, statement (ii) is correct.***
 
• **Analysis of Statement (iii)**: The **Standard International (S.I.) unit** of work is the **Joule (J)**. One Joule is defined as the amount of work done when a force of **1 Newton** displaces an object by **1 meter** in the direction of the force. ***Hence, statement (iii) is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both (ii) and (iii).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Work**: 
 
 
• **Work** is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has only magnitude and no direction, even though it is the dot product of two **vector quantities** (force and displacement).
 
• **Negative Work**: Work is considered negative when the force acts in the **opposite direction** of displacement (angle **θ = 180 degrees**). A primary example is the **force of friction** acting against a moving object.
 
 
 
• **Units and Conversions**:
 
 
• In the **CGS system**, the unit of work is the **erg**.
 
• The relationship between the Joule and the Erg is **1 Joule = 10⁷ ergs**.
 
• The **dimensional formula** for work is **[M1 L2 T-2]**, which is identical to the dimensional formula for **energy** and **torque**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Work in Different Contexts**:
 
 
• **Mechanical Work**: Moving an object against a force.
 
• **Thermodynamic Work**: Often represented as **PΔV** (pressure times change in volume) in gases.
 
• **Electrical Work**: Done when a **charge** is moved through a **potential difference**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: This theorem states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the change in its **kinetic energy**. If the work done is positive, the kinetic energy increases; if negative, the kinetic energy decreases.
 
• **Zero Work Examples**: 
 
 
• A **coolie** carrying a luggage on his head and walking on a horizontal platform does **zero work** against gravity because the force (upward) is perpendicular to the displacement (horizontal).
 
• The **centripetal force** acting on a body in **uniform circular motion** does no work because it is always directed towards the center, perpendicular to the instantaneous displacement.
 
 
 
• **Constant vs. Variable Force**: While the question specifies a **constant force**, it is important to note that if the force **varies** with position, the work done is calculated as the **integral** of force over the displacement (the area under a **Force-Displacement graph**).
</ul
